# STD-APP-COMP-001: Product Module Package Standard

**Standards Metadata**

```yaml
standard_id: 'STD-APP-COMP-001'
standard_name: 'Product Module Package Standard'
standard_type: 'application'
category: 'application'
version: '5.0.0'
status: 'active'
compliance_level: 'mandatory'
tags: ['application', 'module', 'module-bundle', 'portal-studio', 'product-package', 'studio-manifest', 'module-federation', 'webpack', 'remoteEntry', 'contract', 'a11y', 'mandatory']
```

---

> This standard is **additive to [STD-APP-FE-001](../frontend/STD-APP-FE-001-react-application-standards.md)**. Domain teams first build a standard Webpack 5 Module Federation remote per STD-APP-FE-001 — all rules there apply in full. This standard adds the Portal Studio metadata layer (`studio-manifest.json`) that Portal Studio needs to discover, author, theme, and serve each **Module**. **Portal Studio is responsible for working with standard MF remotes. Domain teams are not required to build Portal Studio-specific artifacts** — they build industry-standard remotes and provide a manifest that describes the contract.

[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#11-relationship-to-std-app-fe-001]

### 1.1 Relationship to STD-APP-FE-001

**STD-APP-FE-001 is the build standard.** It defines the Webpack 5 MF remote configuration, TypeScript requirements, component stack (Shadcn/UI + Radix + Tailwind), shared singletons, bundle budget, and test framework. All of those rules apply to Portal Studio modules without modification.

**This standard is additive.** It defines only what Portal Studio additionally requires on top of a compliant STD-APP-FE-001 remote: the `studio-manifest.json` contract metadata that Portal Studio uses to discover, author, theme, localize, and serve each Module.

The onus is on Portal Studio to work with standard Webpack 5 MF remotes. Domain teams build standard remotes first. Portal Studio is a consumer of those remotes — it adapts to them.

page_texts.7:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#13-what-this-standard-covers]

### 1.3 What This Standard Covers

Portal Studio allows product domain teams to register versioned UI Modules via a **Product Package** — a self-contained npm `.tgz` artifact published to a governed JFrog Artifactory registry. Studio discovers, previews, and imports these packages without requiring the domain service to be live.

This standard defines:
- What every Product Package **must** contain in addition to the STD-APP-FE-001 build output
- The canonical `studio-manifest.json` schema and contract requirements
- Rules the Studio compliance gate enforces at import time
- How AI agents should implement the Portal Studio metadata layer

**The canonical JSON Schema** for `studio-manifest.json` is maintained in `mmes-common-core` at `schemas/studio-manifest.v1.schema.json`. The `studio_manifest` concern in `mmes-common-core` provides a validator in Rust, C#, Java, and Python that domain teams can use to validate their manifest before publishing.

> **Schema version note:** The schema file is named `studio-manifest.v1.schema.json` (v1 of the file format). Compliant manifests declare `"schemaVersion": "1.0"`.

page_texts.8:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#20-scope-and-applicability]

## 2.0 Scope and Applicability

This standard applies to:
- All product domain teams publishing UI Modules to Portal Studio (`@mmes` registry)
- AI agents tasked with building Portal Studio Modules in any product domain repository
- CI/CD pipelines that build and publish Product Packages
- The `studio-package-validator` CLI tool

This standard does **not** apply to:
- Platform-scoped Modules built by the Gainwell UI Platform team (different registry, same schema)
- Internal npm libraries not intended for Portal Studio
- Repositories that have explicitly opted out (see § 2.1)
page_texts.9:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#21-opt-out-via-projectyml]

### 2.1 Opt-Out via `.project.yml`

Portal Studio compliance is **enabled by default for all new greenfield repositories** managed via the `eap-bootstrap` scaffold. It is controlled by the `studio_packaging` key in `.project.yml`:

```yaml
# Default for all new repos — Portal Studio compliance is active
studio_packaging: true

# Set to false to opt out — repos with no Portal Studio Modules (e.g. polyglot libraries)
studio_packaging: false
```

When `studio_packaging: false`:
- `arch-health-check` Phase 13 (Product Package Compliance) is **skipped entirely**
- The `/ui-component-create` and `/ui-component-modify` commands still work but will warn that the repo is not configured for Portal Studio publishing
- No `components/react/bundle/studio-manifest.json` or `@mmes/*-studio-webpack` npm package is expected

**Repos that should set `studio_packaging: false`:** polyglot library repos with no Portal Studio Modules (e.g. `mmes-cmn-core`, `mmes-cmn-pipeline` engine library). Repos that deliver UI surfaces to Portal Studio must leave it `true`.

[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#30-package-structure]

## 3.0 Package Structure

Every Product Package **must** conform to this file structure:

```
@mmes/{domain}-{package-name}-studio-webpack-{version}.tgz
└── package/
    ├── package.json                            ← REQUIRED: npm manifest with compliance metadata
    ├── studio-manifest.json                    ← REQUIRED: Studio import manifest (schema v1.0)
    ├── dist/
    │   └── mf/
    │       └── remoteEntry.js                  ← REQUIRED: Webpack 5 MF remote entry (Module Bundle)
    ├── types/
    │   └── {module-name}.d.ts                  ← RECOMMENDED: TypeScript declarations
    ├── thumbs/
    │   ├── {module-name}-light.png             ← RECOMMENDED: 128×128 PNG (light theme)
    │   └── {module-name}-dark.png              ← RECOMMENDED: 128×128 PNG (dark theme)
    └── tests/
        └── {module-name}.cert.ts               ← REQUIRED: certification test suite
```
page_texts.11:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#31-packagejson-required-fields]

### 3.1 `package.json` Required Fields

```json
{
  "name": "@mmes/{domain}-{package-name}-studio-webpack",
  "version": "{semver}",
  "keywords": ["portal-studio-package", "gainwell-portal-compliant"],
  "portalStudio": {
    "schemaVersion": "1.0",
    "productDomain": "{domain-id}",
    "studioCompliant": true
  }
}
```

The `gainwell-portal-compliant` keyword and `portalStudio.studioCompliant: true` are required for the JFrog compliance gate filter. Packages without these fields **will not appear** in Studio's package discovery.

[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#32-naming-conventions]

### 3.2 Naming Conventions

| Element | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Package name | `@mmes/{domain}-{package-name}-studio-webpack` | `@mmes/member-eligibility-studio-webpack` |
| Package version | Semver matching domain service release | `1.4.2` |
| Module namespace | `@{domain-id}/{module-name}` | `@member/member-search` |
| MF remote name | `{domain}_{module}` (underscores — Webpack MF requirement) | `member_memberSearch` |
| `remoteEntry` URL | `https://{cdn-host}/@mmes/{domain}-{package-name}-studio-webpack/-/remoteEntry.js` | See §11 |

## 4.0 studio-manifest.json Schema

The canonical schema is at `mmes-common-core/schemas/studio-manifest.v1.schema.json`. Use the `studio_manifest` concern validator to validate before publishing.

[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#41-required-top-level-fields]

### 4.1 Required Top-Level Fields

| Field | Type | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `schemaVersion` | string | Must be `"1.1"` (or `"1.0"` for legacy packages — see §4.5) |
| `product` | string | Version-free domain ID — unique in registry |
| `displayName` | string | Human-readable product name |
| `description` | string | One-paragraph description |
| `version` | string | Valid semver matching `package.json` version |
| `publishedAt` | string | ISO 8601 datetime |
page_texts.15:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#42-endpoints-array]

### 4.2 Endpoints Array

Each endpoint in `endpoints[]` must declare:

| Field | Required | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | Yes | Unique within product, dot-notation (e.g., `member.search`) |
| `method` | Yes | One of: `GET` `POST` `PUT` `DELETE` `PATCH` |
| `path` | Yes | Relative path; path params use `{paramName}` |
| `description` | Yes | Human-readable description |
| `responseFields` | Recommended | Top-level response field names |
| `queryParams` | Recommended | Accepted query parameter names |
page_texts.16:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#43-modules-array]

### 4.3 Modules Array

Each module in `modules[]` must declare:

| Field | Required |
|---|---|
| `namespace` | Yes — `@{domain-id}/{module-name}` |
| `version` | Yes |
| `displayName` | Yes |
| `description` | Yes |
| `remoteEntry` | Yes — absolute HTTPS URL to `remoteEntry.js` (see §5) |
| `exposedModule` | Yes — Webpack MF exposed module name (e.g., `"./MemberSearch"`) |
| `certificationTestFile` | Yes — must end in `.cert.ts` |
| `a11y` | Yes — see §7.0 |
| `contract` | Yes — see §6.0 |
| `help` | Yes — see §6.5 |
| `packageName` | Recommended — `@mmes/{domain}-{package-name}-studio-webpack` |
| `typesFile` | Recommended |
| `thumbnails` | Recommended — `{ light: "...", dark: "..." }` |
| `platformDependencies` | Conditional — required when typed locale properties present |
page_texts.17:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#45-schema-version]

### 4.5 Schema Version

New manifests must declare `"schemaVersion": "1.1"`. Legacy packages at `"1.0"` remain importable but should be migrated:

| Version | Key additions |
|---|---|
| `"1.0"` | Baseline — inline `help.fields` text, `--{product}-*` style hook namespace, `name` field in styleHooks |
| `"1.1"` | Field-help content slots (`labelSlot`/`tooltipSlot`), `token` field in styleHooks, `default` CSS value, `tooltip` content slot kind, `contract.properties` and `contract.events` required, `properties[].type` extended |
page_texts.18:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#44-platform-dependencies]

### 4.4 Platform Dependencies

If a module uses locale-aware formatting, declare:

```json
"platformDependencies": ["@mmes/core/locale_format"]
```

Valid platform dependency identifiers:

| Identifier | When to declare |
|---|---|
| `@mmes/core/locale_format` | Module has typed properties of type `date`, `time`, `datetime`, `currency`, or `number` |
| `@mmes/core/localization` | Module uses dynamic string lookup beyond `contentSlots` |

---
page_texts.20:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#51-format]

### 5.1 Format

All Module Bundles **must** be compiled as **Webpack 5 Module Federation remotes** using `ModuleFederationPlugin`. Each remote produces a `remoteEntry.js` file that the Portal Studio host loads dynamically at runtime via `import(remoteEntryUrl)`.

Webpack configuration requirements are defined in [STD-APP-FE-001 §5.0](../frontend/STD-APP-FE-001-react-application-standards.md#50-module-federation-standards) — all rules there apply in full. Portal Studio-specific additions:

- `filename` **must** be exactly `remoteEntry.js` (STD-FE-010)
- Output **must** go to `dist/mf/` within the package
- `name` must follow the `{domain}_{module}` convention (underscores — Webpack MF requirement), e.g. `member_memberSearch`
- One `remoteEntry.js` per Module Bundle — all Modules in the bundle are exposed from the same remote
- `exposes` must contain one entry per declared module: `'./{ModuleName}': './components/{module-name}/src/{ModuleName}'`
page_texts.21:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#52-size-budget]

### 5.2 Size Budget

| Budget | Limit | Measurement |
|---|---|---|
| Per Module | ≤ 500 KB gzipped | Chunk graph loaded when `container.get('./ModuleName')` is called — shared singletons excluded |

The budget is **per Module**, not per `remoteEntry.js` bundle total. A Module Bundle that exposes 10 Modules from one `remoteEntry.js` is compliant as long as each individual Module's chunk graph is ≤ 500 KB when loaded. The `remoteEntry.js` container bootstrap itself is not counted — it is typically < 15 KB.

The certification gate measures each declared Module independently. A package is rejected if any single Module's chunk graph exceeds 500 KB gzipped (shared singletons excluded).
page_texts.22:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#53-shared-dependencies]

### 5.3 Shared Dependencies

React and ReactDOM **must** be declared as `shared` singletons in every Module Bundle. This ensures the shell's React instance is reused — preventing duplicate React contexts, broken hooks, and incompatible concurrent feature behaviour across the shell boundary.

```javascript
shared: {
  react:              { singleton: true, requiredVersion: deps.react },
  'react-dom':        { singleton: true, requiredVersion: deps['react-dom'] },
  'react-router-dom': { singleton: true, requiredVersion: deps['react-router-dom'] },
},
```

**Must NOT** include React or ReactDOM in the bundle itself.
page_texts.23:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#54-theming]

### 5.4 Theming

Modules support both **light and dark themes automatically** by consuming tokens from the Gainwell enterprise design system stylesheet (`@mmes/cmn-core/core-theme.css`). No hardcoded color values. No per-module token namespace for standard UI surfaces.

**Design system token layers:**

| Layer | Tokens | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Primitives** | Raw palette — never used directly in components | `--gainwell-aqua-green`, `--blue-400`, `--neutral-300` |
| **Semantic** | Role-based — consume these in module CSS | `--text-primary`, `--background-primary`, `--widget-border`, `--text-error` |
| **Component** | Sizing constants | `--widget-input-height`, `--font-size-regular`, `--spacing-md` |

**How to consume:**

```css
/* Module CSS — consumes core-theme.css semantic tokens directly */
.my-field { background: var(--background-primary); border: var(--widget-border); }
.my-field label { color: var(--text-primary); font-size: var(--widget-label-font-size); }
.my-field input { height: var(--widget-input-height); font-size: var(--widget-input-font-size); }
.my-field input:focus { outline: var(--widget-focus-outline); }
.my-field .error { color: var(--text-error); border: var(--widget-error-border); }
```

**Theme switching is automatic.** The host shell applies `.theme-light` or `.theme-dark` on a container element. Core-theme.css swaps all semantic token values under those classes. Modules inherit the correct theme with no additional code.

**Module-specific CSS custom properties** are only needed for surfaces not covered by `core-theme.css` (e.g. graph step-status colours, data-visualisation palettes). These go in `contract.styleHooks` — see §6.3.

**The `core-theme.css` import contract:** Modules assume the host has already imported `@mmes/cmn-core/core-theme.css`. In local development and test harnesses, import it explicitly:

```js
import '@mmes/cmn-core/core-theme.css';
```
page_texts.24:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#55-esm-library-build-unchanged]

### 5.5 ESM Library Build (unchanged)

The `@mmes/{name}` ESM library package (built with Vite) used for developer React app consumption continues to be published without modification. Vite remains the ESM library build tool only — it does **not** produce the Module Bundle output.

page_texts.25:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#60-interaction-contract-standards]

## 6.0 Interaction Contract Standards

Every module's `contract` block must include:
page_texts.26:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#61-properties]

### 6.1 Properties

Typed properties **must** declare their type. For locale-formatted values:

```json
{
  "name": "service-date",
  "type": "date",
  "format": "short",
  "description": "Service date — formatted by @mmes/core/locale_format"
}
```

**Type rules:**
- `type: "date" | "time" | "datetime"` → `format` is required (`short | medium | long | full`)
- `type: "currency"` → `currency` is required (ISO 4217, e.g., `"USD"`)
- `type: "number"` → no additional fields required
- `type: "string" | "boolean"` → standard types, no formatting
page_texts.27:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#62-content-slots]

### 6.2 Content Slots

All user-visible strings must be declared as `contentSlots` in English. Studio's AI-assisted translation handles all other locales. No hardcoded UI strings in module render paths.

```json
{
  "key": "searchLabel",
  "kind": "label",
  "description": "Accessible label for the search input",
  "default": "Search members"
}
```

Valid `kind` values: `label` | `tooltip` | `error` | `placeholder` | `heading` | `description` | `action`

**Field-level help as content slots (schemaVersion 1.1+):** For each property in `contract.properties`, declare two content slots — one for the field label and one for the field tooltip/help text:

```json
{ "key": "<module-slug>.field.<property-name>.label",   "kind": "label",   "default": "<en-US label>" },
{ "key": "<module-slug>.field.<property-name>.tooltip", "kind": "tooltip", "default": "<en-US help text>" }
```

Then cross-reference in `help.fields` using slot keys (see §6.5).
page_texts.28:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#63-style-hooks]

### 6.3 Style Hooks

`styleHooks` declares only **module-specific** CSS custom properties — surfaces not covered by `core-theme.css` (see §5.4). Do not redeclare tokens that are already part of the core design system (`--text-*`, `--background-*`, `--widget-*`, `--border-*`, etc.) — Portal Studio overrides those at the core level.

```json
{ "token": "--member-color-status-active", "kind": "cssVar", "default": "#1cab3b", "description": "Status indicator for active members" },
{ "token": "--member-chart-bar-primary",   "kind": "cssVar", "default": "#0062ff", "description": "Primary bar colour in enrolment chart" },
{ "name": "results-list", "kind": "part", "description": "Results container — exposes ::part(results-list)" }
```

Use `token` (preferred) for the CSS custom property name. `name` is accepted for backwards compatibility with schemaVersion 1.0 manifests. Both `token` and `name` fields use `--{product}-*` prefix convention.
page_texts.29:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#64-data-dependencies]

### 6.4 Data Dependencies

Modules that consume backend APIs must declare their endpoint dependencies:

```json
{ "endpointId": "member.search", "description": "Reads member list via BFF proxy" }
```

`endpointId` must reference an endpoint declared in the manifest's `endpoints[]` array.
page_texts.30:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#65-help-content]

### 6.5 Help Content

Every module must declare a `help` block with:
- `description` — 1–3 sentence module summary (localizable)
- `fields` — per-property help metadata (keys match `contract.properties` names)
- `aiHelpContext` — English-only AI grounding prose (never rendered in UI; AI responds in user locale at runtime)

**schemaVersion 1.1+ — slot references (preferred):** `help.fields` values use `labelSlot` and `tooltipSlot` keys that reference content slot entries. This delegates all user-visible text to `contentSlots` so Portal Studio's locale injection pipeline handles translation automatically:

```json
"fields": {
  "serviceDate": {
    "labelSlot": "member-search.field.serviceDate.label",
    "tooltipSlot": "member-search.field.serviceDate.tooltip",
    "example": "2025-01-15"
  }
}
```

**schemaVersion 1.0 — inline text (deprecated, backwards compat only):** `help.fields` values use `label` and `tooltip` as direct en-US strings. These are not locale-injected by Portal Studio and cannot be translated at runtime. Migrate to slot references when updating to schemaVersion 1.1.

---
page_texts.31:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#70-accessibility-standards]

## 7.0 Accessibility Standards

Every module **must** declare an `a11y` block:

```json
{
  "apgPattern": "combobox",
  "wcagConformance": "AA",
  "notes": "Search input uses combobox pattern; results use aria-live=polite"
}
```

| Field | Required | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `apgPattern` | Yes | ARIA APG pattern name (e.g., `combobox`, `listbox`, `dialog`, `tree`) |
| `wcagConformance` | Yes | Must be `"AA"` or `"AAA"` — `"A"` alone is not acceptable |
| `notes` | Recommended | Plain-text description of keyboard interaction and ARIA usage |

WCAG 2.1 AA is the **minimum** for all Portal Studio Modules. Modules that cannot achieve AA conformance must not be published.

---
page_texts.33:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#81-english-is-the-authoring-locale]

### 8.1 English Is the Authoring Locale

All `contentSlots.default` values, `helpContent` text, and property descriptions must be in English (`en-US`). Studio handles translation to other locales via AI-assisted translation.
page_texts.34:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#82-date-time-currency-and-number-formatting]

### 8.2 Date, Time, Currency, and Number Formatting

Modules **must not** format date, time, currency, or number values directly. Declare the property type in the interaction contract and depend on `@mmes/core/locale_format`:

```json
"platformDependencies": ["@mmes/core/locale_format"]
```

The portal platform injects locale context at mount time. See [GUID-APP-I18N-001](../../../strategy/guidance/application/localization/GUID-APP-I18N-001-locale-formatting-guidance.md) for the full formatting guidance.
page_texts.35:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#83-no-hardcoded-locale-sensitive-values]

### 8.3 No Hardcoded Locale-Sensitive Values

Modules must not contain hardcoded date formats, currency symbols, or number separators. These must be resolved via platform formatting at runtime.

---
page_texts.36:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#90-certification-test-standards]

## 9.0 Certification Test Standards

Every module **must** include a certification test file at `tests/{module-name}.cert.ts`. The certification gate runs these tests at import time. A package that fails certification is not importable.
page_texts.37:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#91-required-test-coverage]

### 9.1 Required Test Coverage

| Test | What it verifies |
|---|---|
| Contract completeness | All declared properties, events, actions are exposed by the module |
| Content slot defaults | All `contentSlots` have non-empty default values |
| Style hook existence | All declared CSS custom properties are accepted without error |
| Bundle size | Module's chunk graph ≤ 500 KB gzipped per module (shared singletons excluded) |
| MF remote loadable | `remoteEntry.js` URL resolves and exposes the declared `exposedModule` |
| WCAG 2.1 AA | axe-core accessibility audit passes with zero violations at AA level |
| Keyboard navigation | Focus order matches declared `focusOrder` |

page_texts.41:
[standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#100-compliance-gate]

## 10.0 Compliance Gate

Studio's compliance gate runs automatically at import time. A package is rejected if:

- `studio-manifest.json` fails validation against `studio-manifest.v1.schema.json`
- `schemaVersion` is not `"1.0"` or `"1.1"`
- Any required field is missing
- Any module's chunk graph exceeds 500 KB gzipped
- Any module's `remoteEntry` URL is not an absolute HTTPS URL
- Any module's `exposedModule` does not begin with `"./"`
- Any module's certification test fails
- `wcagConformance` is not `"AA"` or `"AAA"`
- A typed property of type `date`/`time`/`datetime` lacks `format`
- A typed property of type `currency` lacks `currency`

**Pre-publish validation:** Use the `studio_manifest` concern from `mmes-common-core` or the `studio-package-validator` CLI to validate locally before publishing. Never rely on the Studio compliance gate as the first check.

### 11.2 CI Pipeline Requirements

The domain team CI pipeline must:

1. Build Webpack 5 Module Bundle (`webpack --config webpack.mf.config.cjs`)
2. Run certification tests
3. Validate `studio-manifest.json` via `studio-package-validator` CLI
4. Publish to `@mmes` registry
5. Set JFrog properties: `portal.studio.compliant=true`, `portal.studio.schema.version=1.0`

### 11.3 Versioning

Package version must be semver and match the domain service release version. Breaking changes to the interaction contract require a major version bump.

## 12.0 AI Agent Implementation Guide

When an AI agent is tasked with building a Portal Studio Module for a product domain:

**Step 1 — Build a standard MF remote per STD-APP-FE-001**
The Module Bundle is first an industry-standard Webpack 5 MF remote. All rules in [STD-APP-FE-001](../frontend/STD-APP-FE-001-react-application-standards.md) apply:
- [ ] Webpack 5 + `ModuleFederationPlugin`; `filename: 'remoteEntry.js'`; output to `dist/mf/`
- [ ] `react`, `react-dom`, `react-router-dom` declared as shared singletons
- [ ] TypeScript strict mode
- [ ] Shadcn/UI + Radix + Tailwind component stack
- [ ] ≤ 500 KB gzipped per Module (shared deps excluded)
- [ ] Jest + Playwright tests; axe-core in every module test

**Step 2 — Read the canonical Portal Studio schema**
Reference `mmes-common-core/schemas/studio-manifest.v1.schema.json` for the manifest structure.

**Step 3 — Add the Portal Studio manifest layer**
Use the `/ui-component-create` skill or follow this checklist:
- [ ] Create `studio-manifest.json` with `"schemaVersion": "1.1"`
- [ ] Add module entry to `modules[]` array
- [ ] Declare all typed properties with correct `type`, `format`, `currency` fields
- [ ] Declare all `contentSlots` in English — include `label` and `tooltip` slots for every `contract.properties` entry (keys: `<module-slug>.field.<property-name>.label` / `.tooltip`)
- [ ] Import `@mmes/cmn-core/core-theme.css` in the module harness and dev app; consume `--text-*`, `--background-*`, `--widget-*` etc. for all standard UI surfaces — no per-module token aliases
- [ ] Declare `styleHooks` ONLY for module-specific CSS surfaces not covered by `core-theme.css` (e.g. domain-specific status colours, chart palettes)
- [ ] Declare `a11y.apgPattern` and `a11y.wcagConformance: "AA"`
- [ ] Declare `help` block with `description`, `fields`, and `aiHelpContext`
- [ ] Add `platformDependencies: ["@mmes/core/locale_format"]` if any typed locale properties
- [ ] Write `{module-name}.cert.ts` covering all required tests
- [ ] Generate TypeScript declarations
- [ ] Generate 128×128 PNG thumbnails (light + dark)

**Step 4 — Validate before publishing**
```typescript
import { validate } from '@mmes/core/studio_manifest';
const result = validate(manifestJson);
if (!result.valid) throw new Error(result.errors.map(e => e.message).join('\n'));
```

**Step 5 — Publish**
```bash
npm publish --registry https://gwproductengineering.jfrog.io/artifactory/api/npm/mmes-npm/
```
